alignments.note: Imperative rendered by an English phrasal verb; *up* is the verb's own particle under rule 44 and the head stays on the lexical verb.
Construct dual noun rendered *hands*; the possessive standing before it is the suffix's under rule 18, so the unit is discontinuous in English order only.
Pronominal suffix realized by the possessive *your* (rule 18).

Bare nominal with no preposition and no object marker on it; the supplied *to* states what the nominal contributes and belongs to it under rule 33, and the supplied *the* determines the nominal expression under rule 15. Head on the word carrying the lexeme. The ASV margin offers *Or, in holiness*, which is read and set aside under rule 38: the printed text governs.
Imperative with its subject pronoun written immediately after the verb (rules 17 and 36); no vocative stands in this clause to compete for it.
Object marker; the ASV writes the object bare, so rule 16's default applies.
Divine name as object of the imperative.

review_notes: `קֹדֶשׁ` stands with no preposition and no marker on it, so both the supplied *to* and the supplied *the* join its unit under rules 33 and 15 rather than being marked `added`.
The marginal alternative *Or, in holiness* was read and set aside under rule 38; the printed *to the sanctuary* is what is aligned.
